dedupe_keys.name: bikemaps org crowdsourced cycling collisions near misses hazards and thefts

description: BikeMaps.org is a crowdsourcing tool for global mapping of cycling safety. Citizens add reports of cycling collisions or falls, near misses, hazards and bike thefts on a web map, with details such as whether they were involved, what they were riding, the incident type and the object involved; the map also shows new infrastructure and a Strava ridership layer. The team says only about 30 per cent of bike collision data are collected by official systems, and analyses the reports with GIS and statistics to find hot spots of cycling risk and crime. Registered users can trace a region of interest and receive alerts about new reports there. The project has produced many peer-reviewed papers, for example on crowdsourced crashes and near misses in Canadian cities. Coverage is global but reports are densest where the project has been promoted, notably in Canada. Access is a free web map; reporting and alerts need registration. Caveats: reports are self-selected and unverified, and the pages read do not describe a bulk download or a data licence. The reports support hazard exposure and risk studies of cycling networks. They complement the GB STATS19 collision data and Citi Bike trip data catalogued here.
